back: A bend in rock layers produced by compression; upfolds are anticlines, downfolds are synclines.
A fracture in the crust along which the rocks on either side have moved.
Compression pushes rocks together (folds, reverse faults); tension pulls them apart (normal faults).
Simple → asymmetrical → overfold → recumbent → overthrust fold (nappe), as compression increases.
Normal (tension, block slips down), reverse (compression, block pushed up and over), tear (horizontal movement).
A long, steep-sided valley where a block has sunk between two parallel faults, e.g. the East African Rift Valley.
A block left standing high (or pushed up) between two faults, e.g. the Ruwenzori.
The middle Zambezi valley is a faulted trough with the Zambezi escarpment on its southern side; Lake Kariba lies in part of it.
The vertical distance a block has moved along a fault.
